content: 1. Analgesia for pain resulting from perineal trauma following childbirth was reviewed in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2003 (CD003931). 2. Hedayati, Parsons, and Crowther conducted a study on the use of topically applied anesthetics for managing perineal pain after childbirth, published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2005 (CD004223). 3. The 2015 edition of the International Medical Products Price Guide was published by Medical Sciences for Health (MSH) in 2016. 4. The World Health Organization (WHO) released the 21st Model List of Essential Medicines in 2019, providing guidance on critical medications for global health. 5. Briggs, Freeman, and Yaffe authored the eighth edition of Drugs in Pregnancy and Lactation: A Reference Guide to Fetal and Neonatal Risk, published by Lippincott Williams & Wilkins in 2008. 6. Moossdorff-Steinhauser et al. investigated the long-term effects of Motherfit group therapy on stress urinary incontinence in preand post-partum women through two multicenter randomized controlled trials, published in Trials in 2019. 7. Salmon et al. critically analyzed the implementation of pelvic floor muscle training during women's childbearing years, addressing individual, professional, and service-related challenges in Neurourology and Urodynamics in 2020. 8. Hay-Smith et al. reviewed factors influencing adherence to pelvic floor muscle training in primary qualitative studies, as part of the 2011 ICS state-of-the-science seminar, published in Neurourology and Urodynamics in 2015. 9. A fact sheet on responsive feeding, emphasizing the importance of nurturing close and loving relationships, was published to support maternal and child health. 10. The rationale and evidence for the UNICEF UK Baby Friendly Initiative standards were outlined on their official website, accessed on January 20, 2022. 11. Guttman and Zimmerman explored the perspectives of low-income mothers on breastfeeding in a study published in Social Science & Medicine in 2000. 12. Mitra et al. identified predictors of breastfeeding intention among low-income women in a study published in Maternal and Child Health Journal in 2004. 13. Khosravan et al. evaluated the effects of Hollyhock leaf compresses combined with warm and cold compresses on breast engorgement in lactating women in a randomized clinical trial published in the Journal of Evidence-Based Complementary and Alternative Medicine in 2017. 14. Dehghani et al. studied the impact of breast oketani-massage on the severity of breast engorgement, published in the Iranian Journal of Obstetrics, Gynecology, and Infertility in 2017. 15. Lang et al. conducted a cost-consequence analysis of misoprostol for preventing postpartum hemorrhage in low-resource settings, published in BMC Pregnancy and Childbirth in 2015. 16. Gallos et al. performed a network meta-analysis on uterotonic drugs for preventing postpartum hemorrhage, published in Health Technology Assessment in 2019. 17. Bhagat, Agarwal, and Roy systematically reviewed the evidence on serratiopeptidase, published in the International Journal of Surgery in 2013. 18. WHO published recommendations on maternal and newborn care for a positive postnatal experience in 2019. 19. Wilson, Woodd, and Benova conducted a systematic review on the incidence and risk factors for lactational mastitis, published in the Journal of Human Lactation in 2020. 20. Higgins and Johanson reviewed the epidemiology of constipation in North America in a study published in the American Journal of Gastroenterology in 2004. 21. Turawa, Musekiwa, and Rohwer reviewed interventions for preventing postpartum constipation, published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2020. 22. WHO published guidelines on protecting, promoting, and supporting breastfeeding in maternity and newborn care facilities in 2017. 23. WHO released guidelines on counseling women to improve breastfeeding practices in 2018. 24. Jahanfar, Ng, and Teng reviewed the use of antibiotics for mastitis in breastfeeding women, published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2013. 25. A WHO fact sheet on healthy diets was accessed on January 20, 2022. 26. WHO published recommendations for the augmentation of labor in 2014. 27. Downe et al. synthesized qualitative evidence on the provision and uptake of routine antenatal services, published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2019. 28. WHO provided recommendations for breastfeeding and maternal medication in the eleventh Model List of Essential Drugs in 2002. 29. WHO published recommendations for the prevention and treatment of maternal peripartum infections in 2015. 30. WHO released guidelines on preventive chemotherapy for controlling soil-transmitted helminth infections in at-risk populations in 2017. 31. WHO published a guideline on the control and elimination of human schistosomiasis in 2022. 32. Fisher et al. reviewed the prevalence and determinants of common perinatal mental disorders in women in lowand lower-middle-income countries, published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2012. 33. Muzik, Thelen, and Rosenblum discussed the detection and treatment of perinatal depression in a study published in Neuropsychiatry in 2011. 34. Andermann et al. revisited Wilson and Jungner's screening criteria in the genomic age, published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2008. 35. Waqas et al. reviewed evidence on screening programs for common maternal mental health disorders among perinatal women, published in BMC Psychiatry in 2022. 36. Morrell et al. evaluated psychological interventions for postnatal depression in the PoNDER trial, published in Health Technology Assessment in 2009. 37. WHO and the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation published a report on the social determinants of mental health in 2014. 38. Smith, Portela, and Harvey conducted a scoping review of global policies and guidelines on discharge preparation and readiness after birth, published in BMC Pregnancy and Childbirth. 39. Armstrong and Small explored rural women's views on screening for postnatal depression, published in BMC Public Health in 2010. 40. Buist et al. assessed the acceptability of routine screening for perinatal depression, published in the Journal of Affective Disorders in 2006. 41. Waqas et al. critically reviewed and conducted a meta-analysis on the prevention of common mental disorders among women in the perinatal period, published in Global Mental Health. 42. Dukhovny et al. conducted an economic evaluation of a peer support intervention for preventing postpartum depression among high-risk women in Ontario, Canada, published in the American Journal of Perinatology in 2013. 43. Ride et al. evaluated the cost-effectiveness of a psychoeducational intervention for preventing postnatal maternal mental health problems, published in BMJ Open in 2016. 44. Delaney et al. examined the postpartum mental health needs of mothers beyond postpartum depression, published in Issues in Mental Health Nursing in 2015. 45. Raymond et al. conducted a focus group study addressing perinatal depression in underserved urban women, published in BMC Pregnancy and Childbirth in 2014. 46. Thurtle explored first-time mothers' perceptions of motherhood and postnatal depression, published in Community Practitioner in 2003. 47. WHO published guidelines on iron supplementation in postpartum women in 2016. 48. WHO released recommendations on daily iron supplementation for adult women and adolescent girls in 2016. 49. WHO published guidelines on intermittent iron and folic acid supplementation in menstruating women in 2011. 50. WHO provided guidance on hemoglobin concentrations for diagnosing anemia and assessing severity in 2011. 51. The International Nutritional Anemia Consultative Group, WHO, and UNICEF published guidelines for using iron supplements to prevent and treat iron deficiency anemia in 1998. 52. WHO released a booklet on healthy eating during pregnancy and breastfeeding for mothers in 2001. 53. WHO published guidelines on vitamin A supplementation in postpartum women in 2011. 54. WHO released guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behavior in 2020. 55. WHO provided guidance on ensuring human rights in the provision of contraceptive information and services in 2014. 56. WHO published medical eligibility criteria for contraceptive use in 2015. 57. WHO released recommendations on contraceptive eligibility for women at high risk of HIV in 2019. 58. WHO consolidated guidelines on self-care interventions for health, focusing on sexual and reproductive health and rights, in 2019. 59. Rahi and Gilbert reviewed the epidemiology and global impact of visual impairment in children in Taylor and Hoyt’s Pediatric Ophthalmology and Strabismus, sixth edition, published in 2017. 60. WHO published recommendations on maternal and newborn care for a positive postnatal experience in 2019. 61. Malik et al. conducted a systematic review on universal newborn eye screening and international guidelines. 62. Lieu et al. reviewed hearing loss in children, published in JAMA in 2020. 63. Butcher et al. analyzed the prevalence of permanent childhood hearing loss detected through universal newborn hearing screening, published in PLoS One in 2019. 64. WHO released the World Report on Hearing in 2021. 65. Bhutani et al. estimated the incidence and impairment of neonatal hyperbilirubinemia and Rhesus disease of the newborn at regional and global levels in 2010, published in Pediatric Research in 2013. 66. Olusanya, Kaplan, and Hansen provided a global perspective on neonatal hyperbilirubinemia, published in The Lancet Child & Adolescent Health in 2018. 67. Sun et al. evaluated the sensitivity and specificity of the red reflex test in newborn eye screening, published in the Journal of Pediatrics. 68. Haargaard et al. analyzed the age at detection of congenital cataract in the Pediatric Cataract Register (PECaR), published in Acta Ophthalmologica in 2015. 69. Magnusson and Persson conducted a cost-consequence analysis of screening for congenital cataracts at maternity wards versus well-baby clinics, published in Acta Paediatrica in 2005. 70. The American Academy of Pediatrics published guidelines on red reflex examination in neonates, infants, and children in Pediatrics in 2008. 71. UNICEF's supply catalog was accessed on January 20, 2022. 72. Lowe et al. evaluated the Arclight ophthalmoscope as a reliable low-cost alternative to the standard direct ophthalmoscope, published in the Journal of Ophthalmology in 2015. 73. Kong et al. provided an update on the progress and changing epidemiology of childhood blindness worldwide, published in JAAPOS in 2012. 74. Gilbert and Lepvrier-Chomette reviewed gender inequalities in surgery for bilateral cataract among children in low-income countries, published in Ophthalmology in 2016. 75. The Global Retinoblastoma Study Group analyzed global retinoblastoma presentation by national income level, published in JAMA Oncology in 2020. 76. Malik et al. integrated eye health training into the primary child healthcare program in Tanzania, published in BMJ Paediatrics Open in 2020. 77. Mndeme et al. studied the feasibility and diagnostic accuracy of red reflex examination for early detection of pediatric cataract and ocular media disorders in Tanzania, published in Eye in 2021. 78. The Universal Newborn Hearing Screening (UNHS) review group is preparing a systematic review and meta-analysis on the effectiveness of universal newborn hearing screening. 79. Nelson et al. updated the 2001 US Preventive Services Task Force recommendation on universal newborn hearing screening, published in Pediatrics in 2008. 80. Patel et al. reviewed universal newborn hearing screening in Paediatrics & Child Health in 2011. 81. Sharma et al. conducted a systematic review and critique of economic evaluations of childhood hearing loss screening programs, published in Applied Health Economics in 2019. 82. Olusanya et al. analyzed the costs and performance of early hearing detection programs in Lagos, Nigeria, published in Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2009. 83. Heidari et al. conducted a cost-effectiveness analysis of automated auditory brainstem response and otoacoustic emission in universal neonatal hearing screening, published in the Iranian Journal of Pediatrics in 2017. 84. Gupta et al. reviewed the economic evaluations of neonatal hearing screening programs.
